turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Come through. I'm Doctor Hale. What's brought you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's nothing, honestly. I just, um, found a lump. In the shower.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): A lump, whereabouts?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Left breast. Tiny thing. I keep forgetting it's even there.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She nearly cancelled on you. I had to walk her to the car.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it hurt when you press it, or is it painless?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Painless. Completely. If it doesn't hurt it can't be much, can it.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you first notice it?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): My mum had breast cancer and she was in bits, and I don't want to waste a whole appointment if it's just a cyst.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): I hear you. When did you first feel this lump, though?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Sorry. About two weeks ago. Well, actually, might be a bit over, but about two weeks. Soapy hands in the shower and there it was.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any nipple discharge, blood or clear?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. Nipple looks the same as ever.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest's fine.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your weight, any loss?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I don't know really, jeans fit the same I think. Scales at home are ancient. Haven't been trying.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Any regular medicines?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Hasn't got bigger, if that's what you mean. Same little pea.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's handy, but I meant tablets. Anything every day?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, err, just the blood pressure one. Ramepril, five milligrams, I swallow it in the morning.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ramipril five mg each morning for the blood pressure. Anything you've stopped?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Came off the cerazette about a year back. Didn't suit me. Nothing else.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Penicillin. Comes out in a rash. Years ago, and I stay away from it.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your mum's breast cancer, how old was she?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty five. She had the op and the chemo. Still about, still nagging.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Can't stand the smell of it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Getting here was the hard bit, mind. Rain like stair rods all down the ring road.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): And the cricket blaring on the radio. England collapsing again and he would not turn it off.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha. Catch who was bowling?
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Some tall lad, I don't follow it. My grandson kept texting, he's got a match on Sunday if that pitch isn't a puddle.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): They'll be playing in wellies at this rate. We just sat there watching it bucket down.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Typical. Right, pop behind the curtain and I'll have a look.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Arms up for me. Skin on the left looks normal, no dimpling, and the nipple isn't pulled in.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): See. Barely there.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can feel it though. Upper outer part of the left breast, firm lump, about two centimetres, it moves under the fingers, and it isn't tender. Right side feels clear. No glands under either arm.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Two centimetres is nothing. People have bigger peas than that.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Small, yes. Thinking aloud, plenty of lumps like this are a cyst or a fibroadenoma, both benign. I still can't exclude a cancer, though, not at forty six with your mum diagnosed at fifty five.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh please. She was fifty five, I'm not, and mine doesn't hurt.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain's a rotten guide. Most early breast cancers don't hurt, so I'm not sitting on this.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm referring you today on the urgent two-week breast clinic pathway. They usually do a mammogram and an ultrasound when they see you. I won't start any tablets.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. Fine. If I absolutely must.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the skin goes red or the lump suddenly grows before they see you, come back and see me. And don't talk yourself out of going.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

omissions.text: Patient reported the lump has not got bigger and remains the same size ('same little pea').
Weight loss was asked about and not confirmed: patient was unsure, said jeans fit the same, home scales are old, and she has not been trying to lose weight.
Cerazette was discontinued about a year ago because it 'didn't suit' her.
Mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 55 and is still alive after surgery and chemotherapy.
Doctor stated the patient's age as 46 when discussing risk ('not at forty six').
Breast exam additionally found the left breast skin looked normal.
Breast exam additionally found the left breast lump was firm.
Doctor said the breast clinic will usually perform a mammogram and an ultrasound.
Doctor stated no tablets would be started ('I won't start any tablets').
